name: MATLAB
description: MATLAB is a numerical computing environment and programming language built around matrix and array mathematics. It combines an interactive desktop (Command Window, Editor, Live Editor, Workspace and Variable browsers) with a high-level language used for data analysis, linear algebra, signal and image processing, optimization, statistics, ordinary differential equations, visualization and application building. Core MATLAB ships with several thousand built-in functions covering language fundamentals, math, graphics, file I/O, string and date handling, tables and timetables, object-oriented programming, app building with App Designer, and interfaces to C/C++, Fortran, Python, Java, .NET and COM. Add-on toolboxes extend it into specialized domains, but the functions catalogued here are all part of the base MATLAB product.

automation.summary: MATLAB is driven programmatically in four main ways. (1) The MATLAB command line itself: any `.m` script or function can be run headless with `matlab -batch "cmd"` (R2019a and later, the recommended non-interactive entry point) or the older `matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -r "cmd; exit"`. (2) The MATLAB Engine API, which starts or attaches to a MATLAB process from Python, C/C++, Java or .NET and evaluates MATLAB statements and functions from the host language. (3) COM/ActiveX Automation on Windows via the `Matlab.Application` ProgID, which exposes Execute, PutFullMatrix and GetFullMatrix to any COM-capable client. (4) In-process interfaces in the other direction (`py.`, `mex`, `calllib`, `actxserver`, `matlab.net.http`) that let MATLAB call out to Python, C, shared libraries, COM servers and web services. Batch automation typically writes a `.m` script to disk, invokes `matlab -batch`, and reads results back from `.mat`, `.csv`, `.json` or image files.

cli.description: Run MATLAB code non-interactively with no desktop and no splash screen, then exit automatically. Standard output and errors go to the console, the exit code is 0 on success and non-zero if an uncaught error occurs, and no figure windows are shown. This is the recommended way to script MATLAB from a shell, CI job or another program (R2019a and later).
Run a named script file headless. Use `run` (or `cd` first) when the script is not on the MATLAB search path.

Legacy headless invocation. `-nodisplay` suppresses the desktop and X display (Linux/macOS), `-nosplash` skips the splash screen, and `-r` executes the statement. You must call `exit` yourself or the process stays alive; add `-wait` on Windows so the launching shell blocks until MATLAB finishes.
Run with a command-line-only MATLAB and capture the whole session transcript to a log file. Useful when you need the diary of a long batch run.
Set the startup directory with `-sd`, run a function headless and persist the results to a MAT-file that the calling program can read back.
Start without the Java Virtual Machine for the fastest, lightest headless run. Graphics, `uifigure` apps, tables in the Variable Editor and any Java-based I/O are unavailable in this mode.
Compile MATLAB code into a standalone executable with MATLAB Compiler, so it can run on machines without a MATLAB licence (requires the MATLAB Compiler add-on).

apis.name: MATLAB Engine API for Python
apis.description: Starts a MATLAB process from Python and calls MATLAB functions as if they were Python functions. Install with `python -m pip install matlabengine` (version must match the MATLAB release). Data is passed with `matlab.double`, `matlab.int32` and similar array wrappers; `nargout` controls how many outputs are returned. Use `eng.eval` for arbitrary statements and `eng.workspace['x']` to read and write MATLAB workspace variables.
apis.example:
import matlab.engine
eng = matlab.engine.start_matlab()
eng.eval("A = magic(4);", nargout=0)
d = eng.eval("det(A)")
r = eng.rank(matlab.double([[1, 2], [3, 4]]))
eng.workspace['b'] = matlab.double([[1.0], [2.0]])
eng.eval("x = A(1:2,1:2)\\b;", nargout=0)
print(d, r, eng.workspace['x'])
eng.quit()

apis.name: MATLAB Engine API (shared session)
apis.description: Attach to an already running MATLAB desktop instead of starting a new one. In MATLAB run `matlab.engine.shareEngine('myEngine')`, then connect from Python with `connect_matlab`. Useful for driving an interactive session that a user is watching.
apis.example:
import matlab.engine
names = matlab.engine.find_matlab()
eng = matlab.engine.connect_matlab(names[0])
eng.eval("plot(1:10); title('driven from Python')", nargout=0)

apis.name: COM Automation (Windows)
apis.description: MATLAB registers itself as the COM Automation server `Matlab.Application`. Any COM client (Python with pywin32, C#, VBA, Excel) can create the server, send statements with `Execute`, and exchange numeric arrays with `PutFullMatrix`/`GetFullMatrix` or `PutWorkspaceData`/`GetWorkspaceData`. Use the ProgID `Matlab.Application.Single` for a private, non-shared MATLAB instance.
apis.example:
import win32com.client
h = win32com.client.Dispatch('Matlab.Application')
h.Execute("A = magic(4); s = sum(A(:));")
print(h.Execute("disp(s)"))
real, imag = h.GetFullMatrix('A', 'base', [[0]*4]*4, [[0]*4]*4)
h.Execute('quit')

apis.name: MATLAB language (scripts and functions)
apis.description: The primary automation surface is MATLAB code itself. Scripts (`.m`) run statements in the caller's workspace; functions (`.m` with a `function` line) take inputs and return outputs; Live Scripts (`.mlx`) mix code, formatted text and output. `run`, `feval`, `eval` and function handles let one program compose another's behaviour.

apis.name: Python interface inside MATLAB (py.)
apis.description: The reverse direction: MATLAB calls Python libraries in-process through the `py.` namespace. Configure the interpreter with `pyenv`, call modules as `py.module.func(...)`, and run free-form code with `pyrun`/`pyrunfile`. Data is converted automatically for numeric, string and logical types.

apis.name: MEX and C/C++ interfaces
apis.description: `mex` compiles C, C++ or Fortran source into a shared library callable as a MATLAB function, while `loadlibrary`/`calllib` call an existing shared library without writing wrapper code. Use these when you need native speed or must reuse an existing codebase.

apis.name: Web services and HTTP
apis.description: `webread`, `webwrite` and `websave` cover most REST calls with `weboptions` for headers, timeouts and authentication. For full control over verbs, headers, cookies and multipart bodies, use the object-oriented `matlab.net.http` package.

file_formats.description: MATLAB code file: a script, function, or class definition (classdef). Plain UTF-8 text, the unit of reuse and the file type run by `matlab -batch`.

Live Script or Live Function: an Open Packaging Conventions (zip) container holding code, formatted text, equations, images and saved output. Opened in the Live Editor; runnable from the command line with `run` and exportable with `export`.
MATLAB data file storing named workspace variables. Written with `save` and read with `load`; v7.3 files are HDF5-based and support variables larger than 2 GB and partial loading via `matfile`.
Saved MATLAB figure containing the full graphics object hierarchy and data. Written with `savefig`/`saveas` and reopened with `openfig`, so the plot remains editable and zoomable.

App Designer application file: a zip container with the UI layout and the app's classdef code. Created and edited with `appdesigner`, run by typing the app name, and packageable into a standalone app or web app.
Obfuscated (P-coded) MATLAB file produced by `pcode`. Executes like the original `.m` file but the source is not readable; used to distribute code without exposing implementation.
Compiled MEX binary (`.mexw64` on Windows, `.mexa64` on Linux, `.mexmaci64`/`.mexmaca64` on macOS) built with `mex` from C, C++ or Fortran source and called like a normal MATLAB function.
Hardware or add-on support package installer file; double-clicking or running it in MATLAB launches the Add-On installer.
Packaged MATLAB toolbox file produced by the Toolbox packaging tool or `matlab.addons.toolbox.packageToolbox`; installs code, examples and path entries in one step.
MATLAB project, Compiler or Coder project file describing files, dependencies, startup/shutdown scripts and build settings.
